sections.h2: Where the Paulding County recorder is
sections.html:
Paulding County's deeds, mortgages, easements and similar papers are filed and preserved by the recorder. You will find the office in the courthouse, 115 N. Williams Street, in the village of Paulding, which is the county seat.

Searching records on the recorder's website costs nothing directly and works at any hour. Drafting is not something the office does, so a deed that still needs writing should go to your attorney or title agent.

In a typical sale the closing agent takes the deed to be recorded, and you never see it again. Filing it yourself means visiting two offices. The auditor moves the parcel on the tax list, and then the recorder files the instrument.

The recorder's website names three electronic filing vendors: CSC, ePN and Simplifile. Weekday submissions are accepted from 8:00 am until 3:00 pm.

Read the deed carefully before anyone signs it:

  • Your signature needs an acknowledgment taken by an officer named in Revised Code 5301.01, and that officer certifies it.
  • Put the new owner's tax mailing address on the deed and cite the earlier recorded instrument. Both items are used by the auditor under section 319.20.
  • Margins and type should meet state rules, or an added charge follows.

Ohio's usual base price is $34.00 for pages one and two of a deed or mortgage, then $8.00 per page. Counties can layer on a preservation surcharge, capped at $5.00 per document, in an amount of their choosing. A quick call to the recorder gets you the true total before the check is written.

Typical Ohio recording charges under Revised Code 317.32
ChargeAmount
Deed or mortgage, pages one and two$34.00
Every page beyond two$8.00
Layout does not meet state standards$20.00 more
Release or other paper needing a reference$4.00 more per reference
County preservation surchargeUp to $5.00

Documents prepared after June 30, 2009 that miss the standards pick up the extra $20. The standards are type of at least 10 points, black or blue ink only, 3 inches of blank space across the top of page one, and 1 inch of margin on the sides and bottom.

Ten minutes of checking can save a rejected filing.

  • Compare the seller's name with the last recorded deed. A mismatch needs an explanation, either in the deed or in an affidavit.
  • Get the payoff letter from the lender, since a recorded release usually follows payoff.
  • Have the buyer's complete tax mailing address in hand for the auditor's tax list.
  • When only a piece of a tract is being sold, ask the auditor and engineer whether the new description needs sign-off, since each Ohio county sets its own conveyance standards.
  • Write the check for the exact conveyance fee. The auditor says any other amount stalls the transfer.

Attorneys and title agents usually take care of this list. Even a quick cash sale needs each item, so deal with them early.

If you inherited the house or are selling for a relative, the same review applies, with one more question: whose name is on the last recorded deed? The search on the recorder's website will show it. When that name is not the person who is now selling, talk to the title agent before listing, because a gap in the chain of title has to be fixed on the record before a buyer's title company will insure the sale. Bring any old deed, release or easement you have to that conversation.

sections.h2: What the auditor charges on a sale
sections.html:
The auditor gets paid before the deed goes to the recorder. The charges are a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand of the purchase price and a transfer fee of $.50 per parcel.

Your check must match the conveyance fee to the penny, or the transfer stalls. A conveyance calculator under the Tools menu on the auditor's site will run your price for you.

The seller bears this cost under section 319.202(D). Form DTE 100 goes with a standard sale, and DTE 100 (EX) with a claimed exemption. If mineral rights or a manufactured home are part of the sale, the auditor can explain any added steps.

sections.h2: Paulding County housing at a glance
sections.html: Roughly 18,727 people live on about 416 square miles here. Owners live in 80.1% of occupied homes, a home's typical value is $140,800 and typical gross rent is $812 monthly. The July 1, 2025 count was 8,597 housing units, and only 28 building permits were issued in 2025.

Eleven villages dot the county: Antwerp, Broughton, Cecil, Grover Hill, Haviland, Latty, Melrose, Oakwood, Paulding, Payne and Scott. Much of the land is flat farm ground laid out on section roads.

If a farm parcel is divided, the auditor will not transfer the new piece until its description has been reviewed. Check first with the auditor and the county engineer so the legal description is accepted the first time.

sections.h2: From signed deed to recorded deed, step by step
sections.html:
The sequence below shows what is going on while you wait.

  1. An attorney or title agent drafts the deed, because the recorder will not.
  2. You sign in front of a notary or another officer named in section 5301.01.
  3. The auditor collects the conveyance fee and the $.50 per parcel transfer fee, then updates the tax list.
  4. The recorder files the instrument and bills by page.
  5. A lender's release comes later and is recorded against the old mortgage.

A closing agent normally covers steps two through four. Filing in person means bringing the deed, a check for the exact conveyance fee and a separate payment for recording, so phone ahead for the recording total.

sections.h2: Looking up a deed or mortgage release
sections.html:
Begin at the recorder's website, where the records search links to an Ava portal. You can also sign up there for a property fraud alert or a notary fraud alert, which notify you when a document is recorded under a name you register.

Once a mortgage is repaid, a release is recorded. Unsure about an old loan? Look it up before listing, since an open mortgage will surface at closing.

Title companies and investors run the search anyway, so keep your old deed and any release ready.

Heirs sometimes find a recorded document they do not recognize, such as an old easement or a lease. Copy its volume and page or instrument number from the search results so the title agent can read the whole instrument, then ask the recorder's office if the index entry is unclear.

sections.h2: A simpler path when the paperwork is a burden
sections.html: Fee checks, recording and release searches can stretch out a sale. Selling for cash drops the buyer's lender and appraisal, so fewer outsiders must line up. The auditor and recorder are still part of it, and a title agent still handles the deed. Cash Home Buyers CA can list what to gather so the transfer runs on time.

faqs.q: Where does Paulding County keep its land records?
faqs.a: In the courthouse at 115 N. Williams Street in Paulding. The recorder's website hosts the records search as well.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in Paulding County?
faqs.a: Yes, through CSC, ePN or Simplifile, with weekday submissions taken from 8:00 am to 3:00 pm.

faqs.q: What is the county conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor charges $4.00 per thousand of the purchase price plus $.50 per parcel. A calculator on the auditor's site will figure it for your price.

faqs.q: Will the recorder draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. Recording is all the office does, so have an attorney or title company prepare it.

faqs.q: Why was I charged an extra $20 on a deed?
faqs.a: Revised Code 317.114 sets that charge for papers that break the margin, ink or type size rules. Check the layout against the standards before you sign.
